# DebugService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("DebugService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Controls the debug overlay and gives access to the engine's statistics and log. It is available in exported games, with the overlay off unless the game turns it on. The gizmo methods are a development aid and draw nothing in a headless run.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OverlayVisible` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the debug overlay is drawn. It is off by default, including in exported games. |

## Methods

### `CaptureProfile(seconds: number, warmupSeconds: number? = 0): boolean`

Requests a capture of the main thread's CPU scopes, starting and ending at frame boundaries, with durations in seconds of real time. The measurement must be longer than 0 and at most 120 seconds, and the warm-up from 0 to 120 seconds. Returns false while another capture is pending, or for a duration that is out of range or not finite. It is a diagnostic tool; do not use its results in the simulation.

### `DrawBox(cframe: CFrame, size: vector, color: Color3? = nil)`

Draws the wireframe of a box at a `CFrame`, with a size in meters, for one frame. Does nothing in a headless run.

### `DrawLine(a: vector, b: vector, color: Color3? = nil)`

Draws a line between two positions in world space for one frame. Does nothing in a headless run.

### `DrawSphere(position: vector, radius: number, color: Color3? = nil)`

Draws the wireframe of a sphere at a position in world space, with a radius in meters, for one frame. Does nothing in a headless run.

### `GetProfileReport(): any`

Returns the report of the capture requested with `CaptureProfile`, or nil until the capture completes. The report is a table with `frames`, `seconds`, `ticksPerFrame` and `scopes`. Each scope has `name`, `depth`, `meanMs`, `bestMs`, `medianMs`, `p95Ms`, `p99Ms`, `worstMs`, `selfMedianMs`, `calls` and `perCallMs`.

The times are a frame's: what the scope spent in one frame, over the frames captured. `calls` is how many times it ran in a frame, at the median, and `perCallMs` is one run of it. `ticksPerFrame` is how many simulation ticks a frame ran, at the median: 1 for a world keeping up. A server catching up runs several in a frame, and a tick's scopes then show several ticks' time in each frame; read `perCallMs` for one tick.

A scope's times include its child scopes and any waiting, and they are CPU times, not GPU times. At most the latest 16,384 frames are kept. The report stays available until the next capture is requested.

### `GetStat(name: string): number`

Returns the value of a named statistic. The built-in statistics include `FPS`, `FrameTimeMs`, `PhysicsBodies`, `InstanceCount`, `DrawCalls`, `MeshLodDraws`, `LuaMemoryKB` and `ProcessMemoryMB`, and `SetCustomStat` defines more. Raises an error for a name that is not a statistic.

`ProcessMemoryMB` is the memory the whole game's process holds at the moment it is asked, in megabytes, as the operating system counts it: the engine, the graphics driver and the scripts together. 0 where the system does not say.

### `HidePanel(name: string)`

Closes one panel of the debug overlay by name, with the same names as `ShowPanel`. Raises an error for an unknown panel name.

### `SetCustomStat(name: string, value: number)`

Defines or updates a statistic of the game's own under a name. It can then be read with `GetStat` and is shown in the Stats panel. Raises an error if the value is not a number.

### `ShowPanel(name: string)`

Opens one panel of the debug overlay by name. The built-in panels are `Stats`, `Scene`, `Log`, `Streaming`, `Physics` and `Terrain`. The `Terrain` panel shows the terrain's triangles and normals around the camera, in red where a triangle faces the wrong way. Raises an error for an unknown panel name.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `MessageOut(message: string, level: Enum.LogLevel)`

Fires for every console message. Passes the text and its level. Each `print` fires it once with its text at `Info`, and each `warn` once at `Warning`. Engine messages start with their key in square brackets, as in `[scene.err.parent_cycle] ...`, so a handler can match a key to find engine messages. Errors raised in signal handlers are also reported here.
